results.title: Miss Universe Scraps Upper Age Limit,  A Game-Changing Move For Pageants
results.content:
## In a historic move, the upper limit for contestants has been removed from the Miss Universe pageant.

img

In a revelation that shook the beauty pageant world, R'Bonney Gabriel, the current Miss Universe on Thursday, September 15th, 2023 announced that any females above the age of 28 will now be able to participate in the Miss Universe pageant. Earlier the age limit for entering this beauty pageant was 18 to 28 years only. R'Bonney Gabriel made this announcement at designer Tanner Fletcher's "Beauty Pageant" show during New York Fashion Week. Ever since the Miss Universe pageant started in 1952 the age limit for the participants has been 18 to 28 years. R'Bonney, who is now 29 years old, set a new record of her own as the oldest contestant to be crowned Miss Universe when she won the pageant in 2022.

Also Read: Miss Italy Beauty Pageant Says No To Transgender Contestant Entries

Miss Universe's Instagram handle put up a post captioned, "Limitless @rbonneynola closed out Tanner Fletcher's stunning NYFW show as the MISS UNIVERSE Organization announced the elimination of age limits across all MISS UNIVERSE and associated pageants."

According to the reports, while making the announcement, R'Bonney said, "What I love about Miss Universe is that they are always at the forefront, seeking ways to be more inclusive and fulfill the platform they've designed for us. There's a bold, forward-thinking team leading the way here, and many tend to follow our lead. It's an honor to set the standard, and I'm proud that we are making this change."With this path-breaking move, Miss Universe will at once become more inclusive and likely change the pageant game for good. Here's how:

With so many big moves to shake the foundations of conventional beauty standards that have driven decision-making in the pageant world and the beauty industry for decades, it's safe to say that the Miss Universe contest, which begins in November, is a much-anticipated event.

# Miss Universe just made a huge rule change. Now all women 18 and over can compete in the beauty pageant.

By   Anneta Konstantinides

Another huge change is coming to the Miss Universe stage.

R'Bonney Gabriel, the current Miss Universe, said on Tuesday night that the international beauty pageant will now be open to all women aged 18 and over.

The Miss Universe pageant, as well as the Miss USA pageant, previously only permitted contestants between the ages of 18 and 28 to compete.

Gabriel announced the news during designer Tanner Fletcher's 2023 New York Fashion Week show titled "Beauty Pageant," according to Women's Wear Daily.

"What I love about Miss Universe is that they are always out first in line, looking for ways they can be more inclusive and better live up to the platform that they've designed for us," Gabriel told WWD."It's a bold group of women in charge over here, and you know what, a lot of people tend to follow what we do," she added. "It's nice to be a standard-bearer, and I'm proud that we get to do this."

Following Gabriel's announcement, the Miss Universe Organization released a statement on its Instagram story.

2023 Miss Universe pageant with Miss Venezuela, Miss USA, and Miss Dominican Republic.

 

Miss Venezuela, Miss USA, and Miss Dominican Republic at the 2023 Miss Universe pageant.   TIMOTHY A. CLARY/Getty Images

  

"The Miss Universe Organization announces the elimination of all age limits across all Miss Universe and associated pageants," it read. "This change will apply for all 2024 pageants globally. Starting then, every adult woman in the world will be eligible to compete to be in Miss Universe."

While competing for Miss Universe in January, Gabriel said she hoped the Miss Universe Organization would change the age limit.

"I am 28 years old, and that is the oldest age to compete. And I think that's a beautiful thing," Gabriel, who won Miss USA in October, said during the top-five question round."My favorite quote is, 'If not now, then when?"' the former Miss Texas added. "Because as a woman, I believe age does not define us. It's not tomorrow. It's not yesterday. But it's now. The time is now that you can go after what you want."

Gabriel walked the runway at Fletcher's show alongside models who were selected to represent a wide span of ages, according to WWD.

"We are aligned on the belief that all people no matter the societal boxes they have been put into deserve to act as their authentic selves and be celebrated for it," Fletcher Kasell, the cofounder and creative director of Tanner Fletcher, told the site.

Miss USA, R'Bonney Gabriel

 

Gabriel spoke about wanting the age limit to change during the Miss Universe competition.   Josh Brasted/Getty Images

  

Speculation began to swirl around Miss Universe's age requirements after the organization announced in August 2022 that it would begin allowing married women and mothers to compete.

The change took effect in 2023. Miss Maine Juliana Morehouse will make history as the first married woman to compete at Miss USA later this month.

"I've dreamed of getting married for a lot of my life, and I've dreamed of competing at Miss USA for a lot of my life," Morehouse told Insider in May. "I never thought doing the two at the same time would be possible."

Andrea Meza, who was crowned Miss Universe 2020, previously told Insider that the rule change was a long time coming.

#### Marlene Schmidt is the only German woman to have won the Miss Universe crown. She was born in Breslau in 1937, a city that was then part of Germany but now belongs to Poland under the name Wrocław. She grew up in East Germany (the German Democratic Republic) and fled with her family to Stuttgart, West Germany, in 1960.

She pursued a career as a model, actress, screenwriter, and producer. From 1962 to 1965, she was married to American actor Ty Hardin, with whom she had a daughter. In 1969, she married Iraqi-born director and producer Howard Avedis.

Throughout her life, she acted in over 10 films, wrote screenplays for five, and produced 12 films between 1968 and 1987. She became known for her involvement in cult films such as The Stepmother (1972), The Teacher (1974), and Mortuary (1983).

She also served as the model for the Miss Universe logo used from 1963 to 2001.

Now 86 years old, she currently resides in Germany.
